scores.position: STAY on Bunny behind the VideoProvider seam; harden the seam into a real exit ramp (~1.5 engineer-months) and fix the two Bunny settings that cost more than any provider change
scores.strengths: Wins every dimension that was scored except webhook verifiability. (1) THREE-YEAR COST: at the volume that actually exists (docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:3-4 says '60 weddings in SIX MONTHS', i.e. ~10/month, and cost.json scenario[0] prices that at Bunny Rs7,534 vs self-hosted Rs19,971 infra + Rs35,000 people = 7.3x), staying is not close. Over 36 months even at a generous 60/month steady state the rival's own numbers give it ~Rs25k/month of infra saving against Rs70,000/month of headcount it concedes is required - a net loss around Rs16 lakh before the Rs6-9 lakh build. (2) GUEST QUALITY IN INDIA: no change to a 119-PoP Standard tier with Indian presence, which is what the 1.5s-on-4G definition of done rests on; the rival concedes its own origin (B2 US/EU, Hetzner EU) may be SLOWER than Bunny's Singapore origin on the cache-MISS traffic that a 300-guest private catalogue mostly is. (3) DELIVERY RISK: zero. The unattended ops surface already exists - app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:14-124 settles what the webhook loses, app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:52-91 walks a guest path hourly. (4) OPTIONALITY, and this is the sharpest thing in either document: the per-row exit ramp is already half-built and nobody noticed. lib/schema.ts:436 persists titles.provider with default 'bunny', lib/db/seed-data.ts:163 already writes 'fake', and lib/video/index.ts:10-14 getVideoProvider() takes NO ARGUMENT - verified. Ten lines converts any future migration from a flag day plus byte backfill into a per-upload cutover where old films keep serving from Bunny indefinitely. That single change makes the rival's own migration_path step 6 safe, and it costs a week. (5) It correctly identifies the two seam leaks by reading the code rather than trusting the docstring: modules/curated-row/Guest.tsx:27-29 hard-codes 'preview.webp' and components/streaming/useHlsPlayback.ts:123-136 re-appends the token to child URLs under a prefix match - both verified, both exactly the kind of thing that turns 'one line in lib/video/index.ts' into a two-week debug. (6) Its week-5 and week-6 items capture most of the rival's financial case without a transcoder: enforce the 4K allowance per-asset at createUpload (verified unenforced - grep for enabledResolutions/2160/1440 across lib, app, components, modules returns nothing), and move originals to B2 at $6.95/TB behind getDownloadUrl as post-processing at the seam. (7) Honest about what it loses: it names per-catalogue metering as a permanent, genuine loss rather than arguing it away.
scores.weaknesses: Its own headline monthly_infra_inr of Rs11,841 reconciles to nothing in cost.json (not Rs7,534 at 10/month, not Rs45,207 at 60/month) and is unexplained - a sloppy number in a document whose whole argument is arithmetic discipline. It undersells two real costs. First, 'zero dedicated ops headcount' rests on a probe that stops one step short by design (app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:29-31 - verified, the comment says the token is where our responsibility ends), so a Bunny edge fault on a wedding evening is invisible to our alerting; that is a choice, not an absence of risk. Second, its week-6 B2 archive hedge is cheaper than it admits to be tricky: with TUS going straight to Bunny you do not hold the original anywhere else, so getting it to B2 means either a one-time egress copy per wedding (~$3 per 100GB original, still paying back against $12/yr of Bunny storage) or a dual upload that doubles an Indian studio's multi-gigabyte upload - neither is costed. It leaves the photo pull zone's total lack of token auth (N-83) and the webhook blind spot standing, and concedes the rival is right about the latter. Its week-8 'negotiate a committed contract' is correct but is not a plan, it is a hope.

scores.position: BUILD the origin (tusd ingest, FFmpeg ladder, B2 storage, own metering) and keep buying Bunny as a dumb CDN pull zone
scores.strengths: Much the better-argued of the two, and the only honest version of 'build' on the table. 'Own origin, borrowed edge' is the correct shape: it refuses to fight over India-PoP delivery, which is the one line no self-serve alternative beats (CloudFront India $0.109/GB is 3.6x Bunny; Cloudflare's own policy page restricts self-serve video through the CDN). Its arithmetic is reproducible and it leads with its own loss - Rs48,900 vs Bunny's Rs45,207 at the ladder-only profile, a Rs3,700 LOSS, stated up front. It concedes the grant argument outright, which is correct (SISFS Guidelines 8.1.3 bars facilities creation, and commodity transcoding is the opposite of a Novelty claim). Its three correctness findings are real and I verified every one: lib/video/bunny.ts:234-262 derives deliveredGb from watchTimeChart x GB_PER_HOUR.standard and the docstring itself says 'there is no version of this that is measured', with lib/entitlements.ts:119-131 flagging 2.15 as an estimate pending N-24a - so usage_rollup.delivered_gb and the 300GB alert run off an assumption today; the 4K allowance is genuinely unenforceable while resolutions are a library-wide setting; and the webhook target is an account-key-gated dashboard field scripts/preflight.ts structurally cannot assert, which already broke a go-live. The security story is the one place it is strictly better: token parity is exact (the same base64url(sha256(key+path+expires)) directory signing at lib/video/bunny.ts:96-148 signs a Bunny pull zone in front of any origin, so getPlaybackToken is untouched), and it converts an unverifiable webhook into an env var preflight can check. Its migration_path is disciplined - contract freeze, ingest alone as the cheapest place to fail, shadow-mode encoder, demo-catalogue proof against the 1.5s bar, new-weddings-only for a month, 60-day rollback.
scores.weaknesses: Its central number lives at six times the volume that exists. It repeatedly calls 60 weddings/month 'the scale the six-month plan actually targets'; docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:3-4 says '60 weddings in six months' - about 10/month - and cost.json scenario[0] is explicit that at 10/month the fixed floor of a two-box pipeline alone exceeds the entire Bunny bill. The position concedes in costs_and_losses[3] that 'below about 40 weddings/month this decision is straightforwardly wrong', which by its own framing means it is wrong today and for the whole planned horizon. Second, its headline monthly_infra_inr of Rs48,900 omits the Rs70,000/month headcount it elsewhere admits decides the question - the number presented as the cost is not the cost. Third, its strongest financial leg is self-defeating: risks[0] admits the Rs25,000/month storage argument can be tested and mostly captured by turning keep-originals off for one afternoon, and the trade-off it claims that forces (breaking the untouched-originals promise) is weaker than it says - lib/video/bunny.ts:197-210 already asks availableResolutions precisely because 'keep originals is a library setting a future operator could turn off', with a designed honest-fallback label. The rival's B2-archive-at-the-seam gets the same saving with no transcoder. Fourth, it threatens the definition of done it cites: no Indian origin on B2 or Hetzner, cold-cache first play possibly slower than today, mitigated only by a warm-on-publish job that does not exist and is not in the five engineer-months. Fifth, seasonality and blast radius: boxes sized at 1.3x the monthly average against a Nov-Feb cluster, and a stuck encode at 11pm on a Saturday becomes a phone call - it says this plainly, which is to its credit, but it is the cost nobody wants. Sixth, it spends five engineer-months to fix three defects whose cheaper fixes it lists itself (per-asset enabledResolutions at createUpload, per-plan retention as post-processing, a measurement script against getUsage's storageSize). And it is honest that the vendor dependency is not removed - delivery, the largest marginal line at $2.57/wedding, stays on Bunny.

winner: STAY on Bunny behind the VideoProvider seam, executing the seam-hardening plan (per-row provider dispatch, driver-agnostic conformance suite, de-leaking curated-row and useHlsPlayback) plus the two settings fixes - but grafting the build case's target architecture, per-plan retention design, measurement-first step and webhook discipline.
rationale: The two positions agree on more than they admit: both want per-plan retention, both want the 4K allowance enforced in code, both want measured delivery bytes, both keep Bunny as the edge, and both say the highest-severity defect on this subsystem (the Supabase publish gate) outranks the whole argument. They differ only on whether reaching those requires owning the encoder. It does not. The deciding facts are three, and all three are checkable rather than arguable. FIRST, the volume. docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:3-4 targets 60 weddings in SIX MONTHS, about 10 a month; the build case builds its entire Rs25,000/month swing at 60 a month, six times that, and concedes in its own costs_and_losses[3] that below roughly 40/month the decision is straightforwardly wrong. A case that is wrong at today's volume and right at a volume reached in two or three years is an option to hold, not a project to start - and holding it is exactly what the rival proposes. SECOND, the headcount. cost.json finds no breakeven anywhere in 10-1,000 weddings/month once one on-call human is priced, and the build case does not dispute it; it converts the argument into 'are you hiring an SRE anyway'. That is not a transcoding decision, and if the answer is yes the right first project for that person is the Supabase publish gate (lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1390 still filters on published rather than live_at, while the memory driver at lib/db/memory-repository.ts:758 filters liveAt - verified today, photographs were fixed in 7730633 and titles were not) and the four-of-six crons on a scheduler that self-disables, not an FFmpeg ladder. THIRD, and decisively, every benefit the build case claims is reachable from the seam at a fraction of the cost. Per-plan retention: move originals to B2 behind getDownloadUrl as post-processing - no transcoder, no CDN, no on-call. The 4K allowance: set enabledResolutions per asset at createUpload from lib/entitlements - a Bunny per-video API call, not a vendor replacement. Metering: this one genuinely cannot be bought from Bunny and the code says so in its own docstring, so it is a real permanent loss from staying - but it is a commerce-correctness problem worth one engineer-month of instrumentation on the client side and a disputed bill's worth of urgency, not five engineer-months of pipeline. The build case's best contribution is not its conclusion but its architecture: own origin, borrowed edge is the right target if a trigger ever fires, and the rival's plan should be written against it. Meanwhile the rival found the thing neither cost model saw - titles.provider is already persisted (lib/schema.ts:436) and already carries 'fake' in seed data while getVideoProvider() takes no argument (lib/video/index.ts:10-14, verified). Ten lines buys a per-upload cutover with no backfill on the critical path, which is worth more optionality than the entire build buys, and makes the build cheaper and safer if it ever happens. On the scored dimensions: three-year cost, STAY by a wide margin at every volume this business plausibly reaches; delivery risk, STAY (BUILD's own concession that a cold-origin first play may be slower than Bunny's Singapore origin threatens the Phase 0 bar it cites); guest quality in India, STAY; token-auth parity, effectively a draw with a genuine edge to BUILD on webhook verifiability; optionality, STAY, and not narrowly. BUILD earns a 5 rather than a 3 because it is intellectually honest - it leads with its own loss, concedes the grant argument, names the experiment that would kill its best number, and refuses the full-stack version it could have oversold. Those concessions are what make it easy to graft.
disbelieved: BUILD's framing of '60 weddings/month' as 'the scale the six-month plan actually targets'. docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:3-4 reads '60 weddings in six months - 10 of them 4K', i.e. roughly 10 per month; the Rs3,30,000 revenue and Rs55,474 infrastructure in the table at docs/SCALE-PLAN.md:26-36 are six-month cumulative figures, not monthly. The entire Rs25,000/month storage swing sits at 6x the planned volume. cost.json scenario[0] prices the real target and BUILD loses there 2.6x on infrastructure alone, 7.3x including the cheapest ops cover.

BUILD's headline monthly_infra_inr of Rs48,900. The arithmetic is reproducible ($158 B2 + EUR145.50 boxes + $154 Bunny delivery + $29 monitoring = ~$510 = Rs48.8k) but it excludes the Rs70,000/month headcount the same document calls decisive, and it is quoted at a volume that does not exist. The number presented as the cost of building is not the cost of building.

STAY's monthly_infra_inr of Rs11,841. It reconciles to nothing in cost.json - not Rs7,534 (10/month), not Rs45,207 (60/month), not Rs55,474/6 = Rs9,246, not Rs29,689/6 = Rs4,948. Unexplained and unsourced in a document otherwise careful with provenance.

The 3.5x 'originals kept' storage multiplier that both sides lean on. It is derived from a code comment (lib/video/bunny.ts:197-210, which asserts the setting is on) plus docs/PRICING.md section 5's 'renditions approximately 30% on top' - and nobody has read the library's actual stored bytes, even though lib/video/bunny.ts:234-262 already returns video.storageSize per video and a script summing it is an afternoon. BUILD's own triggers_to_revisit[1] concedes the whole financial case flips on this unmeasured number. Treat every storage figure in both documents as provisional until that script runs.

cost.json's most-quoted breakeven, '~50-60 weddings/month on the B2 + Cloudflare stack'. It is produced by a $30/month Cloudflare CDN line for 5 TB of video that cost.json's own assumptions[9] says Cloudflare's policy page forbids on self-serve plans. Price delivery honestly at Bunny's $0.030/GB - as BUILD does - and the 60/month B2 figure moves from Rs36,944 to about Rs48,900, which is ABOVE Bunny's Rs45,207. The headline breakeven is an artefact of a line item the model itself flags as not permitted.

cost.json's Rs35,000/month '0.2 FTE, retained freelancer' at 10 weddings. A retainer does not deliver 11pm-Saturday cover through a Nov-Feb wedding cluster. Either it is too low for what it claims to buy or it buys something narrower than on-call - and it is already larger than the entire Bunny bill at that scale, so the direction of the error only worsens BUILD's case.

The Rs11,000 migration-egress figure both sides quote. 3,800 GB x $0.03 = $114 is arithmetically right, but 3,800 GB is SCALE-PLAN's ladder-only END-OF-YEAR-ONE projection at 10/month, not today's library (today is earlier on that curve), and if keep-originals is really on it is 3-4x larger. The $0.03 Asia CDN rate is also not obviously what Bunny bills for a bulk pull of originals out of Stream. Both the volume and the rate are guesses presented to two significant figures.

BUILD's '5 engineer-months over 4 calendar months'. Its own migration_path sequences roughly 18 weeks of work (1+3+4+3+1+4+2+1) with a dual-run month inside it, and adds an unestimated line it names itself: nothing in this repo has ever measured encode quality, so tuning a first x264 ladder to Bunny's per-delivered-byte quality is open-ended. Four calendar months has no slack in it.

GB_PER_HOUR.standard = 2.15, which is load-bearing on BOTH sides and is marked 'Estimates, not measurements' at lib/entitlements.ts:119-131. cost.json derives '835 source minutes to encode per wedding' from it, every delivered-GB figure inherits it, and BUILD's encoder sizing depends on it. It biases both columns in the same direction, so it does not change the verdict - but no figure in this debate deserves more than one significant figure until N-24a lands.

STAY's implied claim that moving originals to B2 behind getDownloadUrl is free. With TUS uploading straight to Bunny you do not hold the original anywhere else, so the archive copy costs either a one-time egress per wedding or a dual browser upload of a multi-gigabyte file from an Indian studio. It still pays back, but the week-6 line item is not the zero-cost hedge it is written as.
graft_from_losers: Adopt 'own origin, borrowed edge' as the NAMED target architecture, not just a hypothetical. When STAY writes its driver-agnostic conformance suite in weeks 3-4, write it against that specific shape - tusd ingest, FFmpeg ladder emitting playlist.m3u8 + seek/seek.vtt + thumbnail_N.jpg, B2 origin, Bunny pull zone signing with the existing base64url(sha256(key+path+expires)). A suite written against a named target is an exit ramp; one written against an abstraction is a wish.

Take BUILD's per-title retention COLUMN, not just STAY's B2 archive step. Originals kept for Keep and Cinema, ladder-only for Deliver after 30 days, driven by the catalogue's plan. This is the largest single cost lever in either document and it is implementable as post-processing at the seam without a transcoder. STAY's week 6 is the right week; BUILD has the right design for it.

Run BUILD's migration_path step 0 FIRST, before any of STAY's eight weeks: sum video.storageSize across the live library (lib/video/bunny.ts:234-262 already returns it) and read the real stored GB per wedding against the 31.7 GB ladder-only model. Both documents' storage arguments are unmeasured. This is an afternoon and it decides whether week 6 is worth Rs25,000/month or nothing.

Concede BUILD's webhook point and fix the fixable half. The Bunny-side field stays unassertable, so make scripts/preflight.ts assert that OUR endpoint is reachable and correctly signed at the expected URL, print the dashboard value it must match, and put that comparison in the domain-change runbook. The go-live failure mode in docs/GO-LIVE.md:213-244 - uploads succeed, encoding finishes, titles never leave processing, and the webhook answers 200 from superseded code - deserves a check even when the check cannot be automatic.

Extend app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts to fetch one real segment and classify the failure as edge-versus-app, instead of stopping at the token. STAY's 'zero ops headcount' claim rests on a probe that by its own comment (lines 29-31) declines to observe the thing a guest experiences. Bunny's outage is still our wedding.

Keep BUILD's migration DISCIPLINE as the written playbook for the day a trigger fires: contract freeze, ingest alone as the cheapest place to fail, shadow-mode encoder against a copy, prove on the demo catalogue against the 1.5s-on-4G bar with a real handset before anything routes, new weddings only for a full month, 60 clean days before deleting the Bunny library. Write it now while it is cheap, so nobody improvises it at 300 weddings a month.

Record BUILD's grant concession verbatim so the argument does not come back: SISFS Guidelines 8.1.3 bars the seed fund from facilities creation, the ISMC's Novelty criterion scores IP rather than build-versus-buy, and commodity transcoding that Bunny gives away free reads as a cost centre. The defensible novelty is the catalogue, the multi-function capacity and the archive guarantee - none of which depends on who encodes the video.

Adopt BUILD's two commercial triggers as instrumented alarms rather than intuitions: the first month premium 4K encoding exceeds a set rupee figure, and the first customer dispute over a delivered-GB number that turns out to be watch_seconds x 2.15. Both convert this from an architecture argument into a commercial one, and both are measurable from data the system already has.

Before either plan starts: fix lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1390 to gate titles on live_at the way lib/db/memory-repository.ts:758 does and the way photographs now are after 7730633. Both positions name this as outranking the entire debate and both are right; it is the only item here that is currently showing guests content they should not see.
